sourceEvidence.text: Founder approved tenant-scoped shared reminders: view and save, no public release or cross-tenant access.
Participant A says reminders get buried in group chat.
Participant B says different versions of reminder text confuse the household.

Save requires tenant,id,title,expectedVersion,requestId; title trimmed 1–80 chars; create v0, update exact version; replay identical successful tenant/request id, conflict on changed payload, sorted cloned list.

criteria.R1: Problem grounded in fictional sources; source references accurate.
criteria.R2: Hypothesis in approved scope, falsifiable, validation feasible as proposal and not claimed observed.
criteria.R3: Three alternatives including no-build with meaningful tradeoffs; recommendation tied to scope.
criteria.R4: Metric target, unknown baseline and proxy limitation; testable definition.
criteria.R5: Scope boundary and decision consistent, no unapproved commitments or false observed results.
criteria.R6: Arjun handoff pending and review before building; brief accurately represents contract, no invented owners or evidence.

E1.statement: Household reminders are lost in group chat noise and suffer from version drift, causing confusion about the current reminder text.

E2.hypothesis: Tenant users find reminders more discoverable when saved in a dedicated tenant-scoped view versus buried in group chat.
E2.validation: Run A/B test with 200 tenants, measuring % of reminders accessed within 24h; target ≥30% increase over baseline.

E3.reason: Fits approved scope (tenant-view, tenant-save, stale-recovery, duplicate-reconciliation); directly solves burial and version drift with versioned contract (S4); no cross-tenant or public release risk.

Pinning or threading in chat only mitigates burial; does not enforce single source of truth for reminder text, so version drift (S3) persists; also requires chat-platform changes outside product control.
Leaves both burial (S2) and version confusion (S3) unresolved; households continue using unreliable workarounds; no progress on approved tenant-scoped reminder capability.

E6.nextAction: Submit the hypothesis and validation plan to the architecture review board for versioned API design approval before any code is written.

evidence.E7:
# Concept
Household reminders are lost in group chat noise and suffer from version drift, causing confusion about the current reminder text. [S2,S3]
A1 (hypothesis): Tenant users find reminders more discoverable when saved in a dedicated tenant-scoped view versus buried in group chat. Test: Run A/B test with 200 tenants, measuring % of reminders accessed within 24h; target ≥30% increase over baseline.
shared-board (recommended): Fits approved scope (tenant-view, tenant-save, stale-recovery, duplicate-reconciliation); directly solves burial and version drift with versioned contract (S4); no cross-tenant or public release risk.
improve-chat: Pinning or threading in chat only mitigates burial; does not enforce single source of truth for reminder text, so version drift (S3) persists; also requires chat-platform changes outside product control.
no-build: Leaves both burial (S2) and version confusion (S3) unresolved; households continue using unreliable workarounds; no progress on approved tenant-scoped reminder capability.
Metric reminder-saved-and-visible: 80% / 14d / 50 samples; confirmed-visible-saves/eligible-save-attempts; baseline unknown; proxy, not observed impact.
Scope: tenant-view,tenant-save,stale-recovery,duplicate-reconciliation; excludes cross-tenant,offline-write,real-notifications,public-release.
Decision: continue; retain-tenant-isolation.
Handoff arjun-cpto (pending, routine-validation): Submit the hypothesis and validation plan to the architecture review board for versioned API design approval before any code is written.
